messaging.messaging.common.v1.SecurityPr.description: PRIVATE_E2EE: client-side MLS 1.0 encryption, the server holds no decryption key. MANAGED: server-processable, never presented as E2EE.

ciphertext.description: PRIVATE_E2EE: the MLS PrivateMessage (MLSMessage bytes, base64url). Never plaintext.

text.description: MANAGED plain text (UTF-8, 1-16384 characters, no control characters). No markup subset is defined: the server never interprets HTML, Markdown or scripts, stores the text exactly as given and returns it as a JSON string; clients render it as text (escaping it), never as markup.

notify.description: false: no push notification jobs (mirrored / migrated writes). Default true.

managedPresentation.description: MANAGED only (refused for PRIVATE_E2EE, whose presentation travels inside the ciphertext).

mentionedPrincipalIds.description: Section 13, MANAGED only: current ACTIVE members this message mentions (ids only; the sender is ignored; anyone else is VALIDATION_ERROR). PRIVATE_E2EE refuses it (CONTENT_REJECTED / MENTIONS_MANAGED_ONLY): encrypted mentions stay inside the ciphertext. A retry with the same clientMessageId must repeat the text and the attachment set (IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED otherwise) and is answered before rate limits are charged.

messaging.messaging.common.v1.SendMessag.description: Which fields apply is decided by the conversation's PERSISTED security profile: PRIVATE_E2EE needs deviceId, epoch and ciphertext and refuses text (CONTENT_REJECTED / PLAINTEXT_IN_E2EE); MANAGED needs text and refuses ciphertext.

messaging.messaging.common.v1.SmsBridgeD.description: Part V H §106: the disclosure a bridge creator must acknowledge (version-pinned).

messaging.messaging.common.v1.SmsTranspo.description: Carrier state of one bridged message — separate from in-app delivery and read state (§110).

unreadReplyCount.description: Replies from others after the caller's read cursor.

messaging.messaging.common.v1.ThreadSumm.description: §47: a thread's reply count, last reply and the caller's unread replies, counted only inside the caller's history window (active, not hidden).

messaging.messaging.common.v1.ThumbnailG.description: A short-lived read of a MANAGED image's thumbnail, authorized exactly like a download grant of the original.

leafData.description: base64url of the exact leaf bytes the log hashed (canonical JSON).

logId.description: The deployment's key-transparency log (stable across key rotation); signed.

timestamp.description: When this head was produced (RFC 3339, microseconds).

timestampMicros.description: The same instant in Unix microseconds: exactly what the signature covers.

keyId.description: First 8 bytes (hex) of SHA-256 of the log's Ed25519 public key, which clients pin out of band.

signature.description: base64url Ed25519 signature (64 bytes) over the length-prefixed encoding of label 'cfmeet-messaging-kt-tree-head:v1', logId, treeSize (u64 BE), rootHash and timestampMicros (i64 BE) — packages/messaging-crypto transparency::tree_head_signing_input / verify_tree_head_signature (Part V G.5).

witnessStatus.description: WITNESSED only when at least witnessQuorum distinct configured witnesses cosigned exactly this head (verify with packages/messaging-crypto transparency::verify_witnessed_tree_head against witness keys you pin). UNWITNESSED: verifiable but not, by itself, anti-equivocation.

witnessQuorum.description: Distinct witness cosignatures this deployment requires for WITNESSED (0: no witnesses configured).

cosignatures.description: Witness cosignatures of exactly this head (logId, treeSize, rootHash, timestampMicros), each already verified by Messaging under the witness's pinned key; clients verify them again.

messaging.messaging.common.v1.TreeHead.description: A SIGNED tree head (Part V G.5) with the cosignatures of independent key-transparency witnesses (AD-05). The log signing key is a server secret distinct from the service-authentication key. A witness cosigns a head only after verifying the log signature and a consistency proof from the last head it cosigned, so a quorum of witnesses prevents the log from showing different views.

retentionSeconds.description: §90 / disappearing messages: a conversation-specific retention, never looser than the context's (or environment's) retention policy (RETENTION_LOOSER_THAN_POLICY). The retention worker expires older messages (tombstone, then purge unless a legal hold protects them); clients delete locally on the same timer. Audited. Only ever tightens (RETENTION_ONLY_TIGHTENS).

title.description: Section 13: a new display title; null clears it (MANAGED only, owner).

avatarRef.description: Section 13: a new avatar reference; null clears it (MANAGED only, owner).

messaging.messaging.common.v1.UpdateConv.description: Optimistic concurrency on the aggregate version. EXPIRED is set by the server only. A security profile can never be changed (SECURITY_PROFILE_IMMUTABLE).

pricing.description: Messaging records usage facts only; it never prices or bills.

messaging.messaging.common.v1.UsageSumma.description: Usage facts of the caller's application environment (Part V I §129): quantities only, no price, rate or cost.

cosignedAtMicros.description: When the witness cosigned (Unix microseconds); signed.

signature.description: base64url Ed25519 signature over the length-prefixed encoding of label 'cfmeet-messaging-kt-witness-cosignature:v1', witnessId, logId, treeSize (u64 BE), rootHash, timestampMicros (i64 BE) and cosignedAtMicros (i64 BE) — packages/messaging-crypto transparency::witness_cosignature_input.

messaging.messaging.common.v1.WitnessCos.description: One witness's cosignature of a tree head.

messaging.platform.common.v1.RequestId.description: Server-generated identifier of one request / one service hop.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Acquisitio.description: A reservation being (or having been) provisioned for the caller's scope. PROVISIONED means the platform acquired the number — NOT an active customer number (that needs an eligible owner, routing and readiness: a DCN assignment). Provider identifiers and route references never appear.

liveRouting.description: false for synthetic test inventory: never live public routing.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Acquisitio.description: GET /v1/numbers/acquisitions: the caller's acquisitions, newest first.
PROVISIONING until the provider's acquisition is proven (PROVISIONED, with a binding), FAILED on a definite refusal (retryable), UNKNOWN while the outcome is reconciled from read-back (never resent).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.AppealRequ.description: A customer appeal of a restricting / denying / review decision of its own scope.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.AppealStat.description: An appeal is resolved by the next final manual decision.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Assignment.description: One append-only history row of an assignment.
GET /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/routing: the pinned routing revision, the number's routing revision (advanced by every routing change; routing grants are bound to it) and per-family readiness.

DCN assignment states (Part IV D6). ACTIVE is reachable only from ACTIVATING (and back from SUSPENDED) and only once every routed family is READY; one open (not CLOSED) assignment per number. ACTIVE -> CLOSED only by an internal transfer to a successor of the same legal owner (close reason TRANSFERRED_INTERNALLY).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Capability.description: Canonical capability types (Part IV D4). Voice / SMS / MMS are routable (served by a provider binding); the others are number-class attributes.
Where a resolved capability's truth comes from. carrierConfirmed is never true for synthetic inventory.
Why a capability is not supported / not usable (fail closed).

GET /internal/v1/number-resources/{id}/capabilities and GET /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/capabilities: every canonical capability resolved from one consistent snapshot, with the revisions consumers compare to reject stale decisions.
VERIFIED only with evidence (never for synthetic inventory); RESTRICTED / WITHDRAWN / EXPIRED / REVOKED do not grant the capability. REVOKED is re-enabled only by an operator or reconciliation.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CatalogCou.description: GET /v1/numbers/catalog/countries/{countryCode}: the catalog of the caller's inventory class (SANDBOX / TEST: synthetic; PRODUCTION: real).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CatalogSou.description: Where a catalog fact comes from. SYNTHETIC_TEST is test data, never real.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CatalogVer.description: VERIFIED only with evidence; SYNTHETIC exactly for the synthetic catalog. Real numbers need VERIFIED catalog facts.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ConfigureR.description: POST /v1/numbers/acquisitions/{acquisitionId}/routes (Idempotency-Key required): configure the provider routes of these capabilities' families on the current binding.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CostEviden.description: Whether a cost is known from a source.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CountryCat.description: The CURRENT country entry of an inventory class.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CountryCod.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country stated by the inventory source (never inferred).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CountryLis.description: GET /v1/numbers/countries: the supported countries of the caller's inventory class (SANDBOX / TEST: synthetic; PRODUCTION: real, verified).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CreateAcqu.description: POST /v1/numbers/acquisitions (Idempotency-Key required): provision a reservation that holds the number.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CreateAssi.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments (Idempotency-Key required): assign a PROVISIONED acquisition (acquisitionId) or a HELD reservation (reservationId) of the caller to its legal owner. Organizational classes belong to the authenticated organization and name no owner; PERSONAL / PROFESSIONAL name an owning principal Platform Access resolves ACTIVE in the caller's environment.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CreateKycC.description: POST /v1/numbers/kyc/cases (numbers.kyc.manage, optional Idempotency-Key). subjectRef is an opaque CF Meet reference (a principal or organization id) — never personal data.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CreatePort.description: POST /v1/numbers/ports (Idempotency-Key required; NUMBERING_PORTING_ENABLED): port-in names the number and country, port-out the assignment. Ownership evidence is protected KYC evidence ids of the scope.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.CreateRese.description: POST /v1/numbers/reservations (Idempotency-Key required). The scope is the caller's trusted one; a body never names a tenant, application or environment.

capabilities.description: Routable capabilities the number is reserved for; each must be supported (E resolver).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.DcnAssignm.description: A DCN assignment of the caller's trusted scope: the legal owner (immutable on the record), the pinned routing revision and the transfer links (an internal transfer closes the predecessor and opens a successor of the same owner).
GET /v1/numbers/assignments: the caller scope's assignments, newest first (keyset pages, optional status / ownershipClass filters).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.E164.description: A normalized E.164 number. Exposed only by the internal Number Resource view to authorized services; never in events, logs or errors.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.EffectiveC.description: One resolved capability: supported (catalog AND this number's valid evidence) and usable now (supported; routable ones also need an ACTIVE number with an active binding serving them).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Eligibilit.description: A recorded (append-only) eligibility decision with every reason. ELIGIBLE has no reasons and is valid until the earlier of its TTL and the KYC approval expiry; an assignment becomes ELIGIBLE only with such a decision of its own scope.
Eligibility outcomes. Precedence: DENIED > UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY > RISK_RESTRICTED > LIMIT_EXCEEDED > ADDITIONAL_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED > KYC_REQUIRED > PENDING_REVIEW > ELIGIBLE.
Why an eligibility outcome applies (fail closed: unknown is a refusal).
POST /v1/numbers/eligibility (numbers.kyc.read): may this scope request such a number? Evaluation only — never reserves or provisions.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Error.description: The error envelope (Cache-Control: no-store). Never contains a number, provider reference, credential or database text.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ErrorCode.description: Stable error codes. PRECONDITION_FAILED / CONFLICT carry the domain rule in `reason`.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.EvidenceCo.description: Accepted evidence content (minimum data; magic bytes must match).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ExternalVe.description: The fixed wording on every voice / SMS capability. CF Meet never guarantees acceptance by WhatsApp, banks, social platforms or any OTP / third-party verification service.
numbering.numbering.common.v1.ExternalVe.const: Supports voice and SMS where provisioned; third-party verification compatibility varies by service and number type.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.FamilyRead.description: One family of a number: the provider route configured on the CURRENT binding AND acknowledged by the family's consumer.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.HoldBasis.description: Why a reservation holds a number: a domain-level hold (D primitives), a recorded ELIGIBLE decision of the reserving scope, or a temporary hold before eligibility where policy permits it (never PRODUCTION; provisioning always requires eligibility).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.InventoryC.description: Which catalog governs a number: synthetic test inventory has its own catalog, never the real one.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.InventoryR.description: How the inventory behind a search page was obtained: REFRESHED (a provider was asked now), CACHED (asked within the refresh interval), PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE (a provider could not be reached; cached observations only), NOT_CONFIGURED (no provider serves the class, or live telecom is not allowed), NOT_REQUESTED (a later page).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycAppeal.description: An appeal of a REJECTED / REVOKED case (back to UNDER_REVIEW for a human reviewer).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycCase.description: A KYC case of the caller's scope (other scopes' cases are NOT_FOUND). Carries ids, statuses and reason codes only.

requirements.description: The exact requirement snapshot the case was opened against.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycCaseHis.description: GET /v1/numbers/kyc/cases/{caseId}/history: the immutable decision history and appeals.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycDecisio.description: One immutable KYC decision record (one per case revision).
Kinds of immutable KYC decision records.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycEvidenc.description: Evidence METADATA (content is never returned outside the privileged access route; no object key, digest or key id).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycIndicat.description: What the KYC requirements in force say about a search result (Workstream F): UNKNOWN when none are published (eligibility then fails closed).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycRequire.description: GET /v1/numbers/kyc/requirements/{countryCode}/{numberType}/{ownershipClass}: the requirements in force for the caller's inventory class (SANDBOX / TEST: explicitly non-production policies). Unknown mandatory requirements are KYC_REQUIREMENTS_UNKNOWN (422), never an empty list.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.KycStatus.description: The KYC case lifecycle: DRAFT → EVIDENCE_REQUIRED → SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED, with MORE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED, REJECTED, EXPIRED and REVOKED (the same edge set in Rust and SQL; APPROVED → APPROVED is a revalidation renewal).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.LifecycleS.description: The canonical Number Resource lifecycle (Part IV D2). Transitions follow one centralized policy (database function number_lifecycle_allowed). UNKNOWN_PROVIDER_STATE is left only by reconciliation with evidence; irreversible provider actions are never repeated while a resource is in it.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Limitation.description: Closed limitation vocabulary. externalVerification is never a guarantee.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.NumberPool.description: An organizational number pool of the caller's scope (organization-owned numbers only; an assignment is in at most one pool; usage / subscription policies are opaque references).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.NumberReso.description: The canonical CF Meet identity of a public number (Number Resource). Independent of any provider identifier; never changes across provider replacement or porting.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.NumberSear.description: GET /v1/numbers/search: one bounded page of the caller's inventory class (a country is required; keyset cursor bound to the query).

inventory.description: How the inventory behind the page was obtained.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.NumberSear.description: One search result: an OBSERVATION of a canonical Number Resource, never a reservation or a guarantee. Provider identifiers never appear.

items.description: A supported capability with its provenance (synthetic for test inventory; carrierConfirmed only for a verified real provider confirmation).

cost.description: Commercial facts as observed (an estimate until billing evidence exists).

observation.description: Freshness of the observation behind the result.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.NumberType.description: Classification, set only from evidence (never inferred from the E.164 format or from SMS support).
A CURRENT number-type entry (generic: provider applicability is internal). Capabilities in neither list are unknown and treated as unsupported.
GET /v1/numbers/countries/{countryCode}/number-types: the generic number-type entries in force, with their capability metadata.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Offboardin.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/offboarding: an EMPLOYEE_DIRECT number leaves the departing employee — unrouted (no replacement) or routed to a replacement (never the departing employee). The number stays the organization's.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.OwnerKind.description: PRINCIPAL for PERSONAL / PROFESSIONAL numbers; ORGANIZATION for every organizational class.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Ownership.description: The owner of a DCN assignment; immutable on the record (a new owner is a new assignment).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.OwnershipC.description: Provider-independent ownership classes (Part IV D7). An organization-owned number routed to an employee (EMPLOYEE_DIRECT) remains organizational property.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.PoolMember.description: A current member of an organizational pool.

usage.description: ASSIGNED while routed to a target, AVAILABLE while unrouted.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.PoolMember.description: A pool membership (ended memberships are kept as history).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.PortDirect.description: Port-in (to CF Meet) or port-out (away from CF Meet).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.PortEviden.description: Adds ownership evidence to a DOCUMENTS_REQUIRED port request.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.PortReques.description: A port request (the number itself is never returned).
The scope's port requests, newest first.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ProviderCo.description: Durable provider command status. UNKNOWN (the request may have been acted on) leaves only through read-back reconciliation; it is never re-sent blindly.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Quarantine.description: The cooldown of a released number with its policy, review and provider confirmation.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ReasonCode.description: Stable UPPER_SNAKE_CASE reason of a change.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Reassignme.description: POST /v1/numbers/reassignments (Idempotency-Key required): a new owner for a REASSIGNABLE number (completed, provider-confirmed POOL_RETURN quarantine; no open release or provider command). A fresh reservation, assignment, routing revision and route configuration; nothing of the previous owner carries over.
The new assignment (RESERVED; activated once the new routes are READY).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Release.description: An auditable release request (never a delete).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ReleaseNum.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/release (Idempotency-Key required): a scheduled or immediate release run in the mandatory order (grants stopped, voice / SMS routing removed, resources detached, removal confirmed, provider release, quarantine).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ReleasePol.description: POOL_RETURN keeps the number CF Meet-controlled (reassignable after quarantine); PROVIDER_RELINQUISH gives it back to the provider (finally RELEASED, never reassigned); PORTED_OUT is completed by a port-out only.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.ReleaseSta.description: Whether a provider hold was given back. An expired or cancelled reservation does NOT imply a provider release: a held live number stays RESERVED with PENDING release until evidence.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Requiremen.description: What a KYC requirement asks the subject to prove.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Reservatio.description: A reservation of the caller's trusted scope (other scopes: NOT_FOUND). PENDING until the provider hold is confirmed (HELD). Ending it never assumes a provider release: providerReleaseState stays PENDING / UNKNOWN until the provider's release is evidenced.
What a CONVERTED reservation became: taken over by a DCN assignment, or a provisioned acquisition (Workstream I).
GET /v1/numbers/reservations: the caller's reservations, newest first (keyset pages).
PENDING until a provider hold is confirmed (HELD); UNKNOWN when the hold outcome is uncertain. EXPIRED / CANCELLED / CONVERTED / FAILED are final.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Revision.description: Optimistic-concurrency revision: 1 at creation, +1 on every effective change. Writers state the revision they expect; a stale one is VERSION_CONFLICT.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.RiskDecisi.description: An explainable, append-only number risk decision.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.RouteFamil.description: A capability family routed by one provider configuration: VOICE (carried by Telephony) or SMS (carried by the SMS Gateway).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.RouteReadi.description: Why a family is not ready to carry traffic.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.RouteStatu.description: Provider route configuration: REQUESTED, CONFIGURED (provider acknowledgement evidence), FAILED, UNKNOWN (reconciled from read-back), SUPERSEDED.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.RoutingRef.description: The pinned routing profile revision of an assignment.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.RoutingTar.description: A routing target: a kind and, unless NONE, an opaque CF Meet reference.

Where a number routes: one voice and one SMS target (kind NONE: not routed). Validated against the ownership class: a personal / professional number routes to its owner only; an employee's direct line to one employee; organizational classes to their constructs.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.SearchAvai.description: AVAILABLE: offered by a fresh observation (reservable, never guaranteed); STALE: the newest observation expired (not reservable until observed again).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.SmsTargetK.description: SMS routing target (opaque CF Meet ids): a principal, an application, a shared-team or department inbox; bounded by the ownership class.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.SubjectKin.description: Who is verified: an individual for PERSONAL / PROFESSIONAL numbers, an organization for organizational ones.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.SubmitEvid.description: POST /v1/numbers/kyc/cases/{caseId}/evidence (numbers.kyc.manage). Content is sealed (AES-256-GCM, bound to the evidence id) and stored privately; ≤ 5 MiB decoded. The kind must be accepted by a requirement of the case.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.SubmitKycC.description: POST /v1/numbers/kyc/cases/{caseId}/submit: every mandatory requirement needs accepted ACTIVE evidence (else MANDATORY_EVIDENCE_MISSING).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.SuspendReq.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/suspend and POST /v1/admin/number-resources/{id}/suspend: local-first suspension (grants refused and revoked at once, ownership retained), then the provider SUSPEND.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.Suspension.description: A number's suspension with its restoration checks (each true / false) and outcome.
The provider route disable: not required (no adapter), PENDING / CONFIRMED / FAILED / UNKNOWN through the durable command executor, UNSUPPORTED by the adapter.
Who suspended a number: its customer (CUSTOMER / ORGANIZATION, lifted by the customer) or an operator, the risk policy or a provider state drift (lifted by an operator only).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.TransferAs.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/transfer (Idempotency-Key required): within the same legal owner only. Same class: a routing revision. Another class of the same owner: the ACTIVE assignment closes (TRANSFERRED_INTERNALLY) and a successor opens, admitted on a re-evaluated eligibility decision of the new class and activated in the same transaction. A different owner is CROSS_OWNER_TRANSFER_UNSUPPORTED.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.TransferRe.description: The outcome of an internal transfer.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.UpdateRout.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/routing: a new routing revision (same class, same owner). expectedRoutingRevision is the profile revision the caller saw (VERSION_CONFLICT otherwise).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.UsageKind.description: What a usage record measures (internal provider cost evidence, never a customer price).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.UsageSumma.description: GET /v1/numbers/usage: quantities of the caller's scope per number and kind (no costs).

items.description: Usage of one number and kind.

numbering.numbering.common.v1.VerifierKi.description: Who verified: the deterministic test adapter (never in staging / production), the audited manual reviewer, or the system (lifecycle steps).

numbering.numbering.common.v1.VoiceTarge.description: Voice routing target: opaque CF Meet ids of Calling / enterprise constructs (principal, professional identity, endpoint, extension, ring group, queue, IVR, department, shared team, voicemail, approved forwarding), never SIP or provider data. The kinds a number may use are bounded by its ownership class (TARGET_NOT_PERMITTED).

numbering.platform.common.v1.RequestId.description: Server-generated identifier of one request / one service hop.

numbering.platform.common.v1.ServiceId.description: Stable, product-independent identity of a deployable CF Meet backend service, e.g. cfmeet.calling, cfmeet.privacy-relay, cfmeet.telephony, cfmeet.platform-access, cfmeet.numbering, cfmeet.sms-gateway, cfmeet.messaging, cfmeet.developer-platform, cfmeet.api-gateway. Never a wildcard.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Au.description: Immutable Privacy Relay evidence event types.
Safe intent metadata of an authorization request.
Normalized platform reason of a decision (no consumer-specific reasons).

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Co.description: Communication channel. VOICE is executed; MESSAGING may be declared for the future and is never executed by sections 26-30 (no chat, SMS or provider messaging).
Lifecycle of a Communication Context. REVOKED and EXPIRED are terminal; COMPLETED never returns to ACTIVE or SUSPENDED.
Route an authorization asks for. Only APPLICATION is executable today.
The typed, bounded context policy (never an arbitrary document). Defaults are fail-safe.

terminateActiveCallsOnRevoke.description: On revoke, actively terminate protected calls (new authority is denied regardless).

terminateActiveCallsOnParticipantRemoval.description: On participant removal, terminate protected calls involving the removed participant; when false they may continue but no new protected call or transfer involving that participant is authorized.

terminateActiveCallsOnSuspend.description: On suspend, terminate protected calls (new authority is denied regardless).

graceAllowsNewCalls.description: Whether new calls may be authorized during the completion grace period.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Di.description: BIDIRECTIONAL: any two active participants, both directions. EXPLICIT: only directed edges authorize; A -> B never implies B -> A.
A directed edge between two subjects; channel restricts it to one channel (absent: every allowed channel).

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.En.description: Active-call enforcement of a mutation (event ids of the durable enforcement jobs it created).
Why active protected calls are enforced against.
Active-call enforcement state of a mutation: NOT_REQUIRED, PENDING (durably queued; Calling has not confirmed) or APPLIED (Calling confirmed). Never claimed before Calling confirms.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Er.description: Stable error codes of the Privacy Relay API. AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE and RATE_LIMITED come from the authenticated platform ingress; INTERNAL_* only from internal routes (never relayed to customers).
Error response body: stable code, fixed safe message, server request id. Never database errors, foreign-resource existence, tokens or contact data.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Ex.description: Consumer-defined, opaque, bounded reference of the business relationship (CF Meet never parses it). It can never be contact data: no telephone number, e-mail address or tel / sip / mailto URI.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Id.description: Client-chosen key: 1-255 printable ASCII characters without spaces.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Pr.description: Lifecycle of a Privacy Relay Session (same graph as contexts); a session never outlives its context's authority.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Re.description: Relay strategy: policy, not proof that a route exists. Every strategy permits the application route; the public-network and callback strategies only become executable when relay-number and telephony infrastructure exists.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Sn.description: Whether a relay session follows its context (INHERITED) or was explicitly narrowed (NARROWED).

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Su.description: Exactly one opaque subject reference: a CF Meet principal id or an opaque ContactReference id. A ContactReference is never a telephone number, e-mail address or SIP URI, and Privacy Relay never resolves it (Contact Vault is a later section).

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.common.v1.Ve.description: Monotonic version (starts at 1, +1 per accepted authority change).

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.contact-dele.description: A short-lived (default 120 s, at most 300 s) Contact Vault access token, returned once (Cache-Control: no-store).
POST /v1/privacy-relay/contact-access-grants (platform credential). Contains no telephone number.
Contact Vault scopes. A credential can delegate only scopes it holds, and Privacy Relay accepts only scopes its contact delegation trust bundle allows the issuer to delegate.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.context.v1.C.description: Safe representation of a Communication Context. Never a telephone number, provider id, carrier, Contact Vault material, service token or customer credential.

effectiveStatus.description: Status at read time: EXPIRED once the final validity has passed, even before the expiry worker materializes it.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.context.v1.C.description: Privacy-safe support evidence: lifecycle, versions, participant and direction history, sessions, recent decisions, audit events and enforcement status. No contact values.

Create a Communication Context (Idempotency-Key required). Scope comes only from the authenticated credential; status, version, authorization results, telephone numbers, providers and relay numbers are not inputs.

directions.description: Required (non-empty) with EXPLICIT; refused with BIDIRECTIONAL.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.context.v1.L.description: Body of an explicit lifecycle command (suspend, resume, complete, revoke). Idempotency-Key required.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.context.v1.U.description: Typed, versioned configuration update (never a status patch or arbitrary merge patch). Absent members are unchanged; participants and directions replace the whole set (participant reassignment keeps the same context). At least one change is required.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.events.v1.Ev.description: Bounded safe evidence: snake_case keys never naming secrets or contact data; ids, versions, counts, statuses.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.evidence.v1..description: Privacy-safe support / dispute evidence of one protected Call, from Calling's own records. Never a telephone number (raw or masked), Contact Vault material, provider / carrier identifier, provider payload, SIP dialog or credential.

oneOf.description: CF Meet normalized failure category (never a vendor status).
Calling's authoritative connected time (first CONNECTED to the end, or durationsAsOf); null when never connected. Never requestedAt -> endedAt.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.evidence.v1..description: One attempt: timing and normalized outcome only (no provider, route secret or destination).

oneOf.description: CF Meet normalized failure category (never a vendor status).

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.evidence.v1..description: A Privacy Relay authorization the Call relied on (ids and versions only).

connectedDurationMs.description: Union of the participant's session connection intervals.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.evidence.v1..description: GET /v1/privacy-relay/sessions/{relay_session_id}/evidence: the protected Calls of one Relay Session (newest first, keyset pages of at most 100).

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.session.v1.C.description: Create a Privacy Relay Session of a context (Idempotency-Key required). Everything except relayStrategy is optional and can only NARROW the context (participants, channels, directions, validity, a strategy among the context's allowed strategies). A relay identity or telephone number is never an input.

privacy_relay.privacy-relay.session.v1.P.description: Safe representation of a Privacy Relay Session (NOT a call; one session may authorize many call attempts). relayIdentityBindingRef is opaque and server-owned (never a number, carrier or provider resource).

executableRoutes.description: Routes the strategy permits that CF Meet can execute today.

sms.platform.common.v1.RequestId.description: Server-generated identifier of one request / one service hop.

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.Cost.description: Estimated / provider-confirmed cost in minor units.

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.Encoding.description: GSM-7 (160 / 153 septets per segment; extension characters count two) or UCS-2 (70 / 67 UTF-16 units).

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.Message.description: One message (inbound or outbound). `content` is the plaintext for the owning environment only (null once purged by retention); the remote party is masked; no provider identifier.

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.MessagePage.description: A page of messages, newest first.

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.OptOutRequest.description: POST /v1/sms/opt-outs (scope sms.send): the customer blocks a recipient for one number (or every number of the environment).

masked.description: The remote party, masked: `+***` and the last four digits. The full number is never returned.

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.Routing.description: Numbering's SMS routing target of an inbound message (opaque CF Meet reference).

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.SendMessageReq.description: POST /v1/sms/messages (scope sms.send, Idempotency-Key required): send ONE message from a Number Resource the environment actively owns (Numbering issues and the gateway consumes a single-use SMS_SENDER grant — an arbitrary sender id is impossible). The recipient is either `to` (E.164) or the remote party of `threadId`.

principalId.description: The principal the message is sent for (required for personal / professional numbers; must be ACTIVE in the environment).

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.Status.description: Transport status. UNKNOWN: the provider may hold the message; it is never resubmitted, only provider evidence resolves it.

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.Thread.description: A transport thread: the messages between one Number Resource and one remote party. A transport index, not a conversation.

sms.sms-gateway.common.v1.ThreadPage.description: A page of threads, most recent first.

calling.platformCredential.description: Customer platform API credential issued to an application environment's service account. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. The roles listed in an operation's security requirement are the platform scopes the credential must hold (e.g. calls.read). Never accepted on internal routes.

calling.signalingCredential.description: Short-lived Call Signaling Credential of one endpoint of one principal (POST /v1/calling/signaling-credentials), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. It authenticates only that endpoint's own signaling operations and is re-checked against the endpoint, the principal and the minting credential on every use. Platform API credentials (cfmk_...) and internal service tokens are refused on these routes. Browsers, which cannot set headers on a WebSocket, offer it on GET /v1/calling/signaling as the subprotocol pair `cfmeet.signaling.v1, bearer.<credential>`.

communications.bearer_auth.description: Existing CF Meet registered account access token from email/password or Google authentication. Never an internal service credential.

developer_platform.platformCredential.description: A Platform Access API credential (server-side only; never in a browser).

developer_platform.userSession.description: The signed-in developer's CF Meet session (Developer Console). Never a machine credential.

gateway.platformCredential.description: A CF Meet API credential issued by Platform Access (Authorization: Bearer). X-CF-* headers supplied by a client are stripped; a client X-CF-Service-Authorization is refused.

meetings.platformCredential.description: Customer platform API credential issued to an application environment's service account, sent to the CF Meet public API Gateway as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. The roles listed in an operation's security requirement are the platform scopes the credential must hold (meetings.read / meetings.write). The gateway forwards the request without the credential; the Meeting Service has Platform Access re-verify it and acts as the environment's machine caller, which manages only meetings owned by its own application environment (any other meeting is 404). Never accepted on internal routes.

messaging.clientToken.name: Authorization
messaging.clientToken.description: CF-Client-Token <Messaging Client Access Token> (device-direct, §105). Accepted by POST /v1/realtime/tickets and, as an alternative to customerCredential, by the member operations that list it: the token's session (device ACTIVE, session ACTIVE and unexpired, principal ACTIVE) is the caller, acting only for its own principal and own device (CF-Acting-Principal may only repeat it). Every other operation answers 401 CLIENT_TOKENS_NOT_ENABLED.

messaging.customerCredential.description: A CF Meet API credential, verified by Platform Access (never by Messaging).

messaging.realtimeTicket.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
messaging.realtimeTicket.description: `cfmeet.messaging.v1, cfmeet.ticket.<ticket>`: the single-use ticket travels as a subprotocol entry; the server answers `cfmeet.messaging.v1` only.

numbering.customerCredential.description: A CF Meet API credential, verified by Platform Access (never by Numbering).

privacy_relay.platformCredential.description: Customer platform API credential (Authorization: Bearer). The roles in an operation's security requirement are the platform scopes the credential must hold (privacy.contexts.read / .write, privacy.sessions.read / .write, privacy.evidence.read).

sms.customerCredential.description: A CF Meet API credential, verified by Platform Access (never by the SMS Gateway).

calling.IdempotencyKey.name: idempotency-key
calling.IdempotencyKey.description: Client-chosen key (1-255 printable ASCII characters, no spaces), sent once. The same key with the same request returns the recorded response; with a different request it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; concurrent duplicates take effect once.

calling.IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: idempotency-key
calling.IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Required. Client-chosen key (1-255 printable ASCII characters, no spaces), sent once. The same key with the same request returns the recorded response (no second call or transfer); with a different request it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

developer_platform.IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
developer_platform.IdempotencyKey.description: Replays return the original response; reuse with a different request is IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. One-time secrets are never replayed.

numbering.IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
numbering.IdempotencyKey.description: Replays of the same request with the same key return the stored outcome; a different request with the key is IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (422).

privacy_relay.Cursor.name: cursor
privacy_relay.Cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor (nextCursor of the previous page).

privacy_relay.IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: idempotency-key
privacy_relay.IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Required on every mutation. Same key + same request: recorded response; different request: 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; concurrent duplicates take effect once.

calling.IdempotentReplayed.description: Present when the response is the recorded response of an earlier identical command (same Idempotency-Key).

developer_platform.IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when the response is the stored result of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key (no new effect).

privacy_relay.IdempotentReplayed.description: true when the response replays an earlier identical request.

calling.AuthenticationFailed.description: Missing, malformed, unknown, revoked, expired or otherwise unusable credential; uniform for every reason. Code AUTHENTICATION_FAILED.

calling.CommandConflict.description: The command cannot apply to the current state: STALE_CALL_VERSION (expectedVersion is not the current version), CALL_STATE_CONFLICT, CALL_RESOURCE_STATE_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (same key, different request), CONFLICT (the command with this key is still in progress), INVITATION_NOT_ACTIONABLE, ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE (another device of the participant won) or TARGET_UNAVAILABLE.

calling.EnterpriseConflict.description: VERSION_CONFLICT (expectedVersion is not the current version; nothing changed) or CONFLICT (an active name / extension number already exists, the resource is disabled, or it is still referenced).

calling.EnterpriseForbidden.description: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE (the credential lacks the operation's enterprise scope; calls.* never implies it) or ENTERPRISE_POLICY_DENIED (the organization's enterprise policy does not grant this capability or action).

calling.Forbidden.description: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE (the credential lacks the operation's scope) or CALL_NOT_AUTHORIZED (the call policy denied the call).

www-authenticate.description: Bearer challenge naming the required scope (INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE only).

calling.InsufficientScope.description: The credential lacks the operation's required scope. Code INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE.

www-authenticate.description: Bearer challenge naming the required scope.

calling.InvalidRequest.description: Malformed or unknown body field, invalid query parameter, or a missing / malformed / repeated Idempotency-Key. Code VALIDATION_ERROR.

calling.InvitationExpired.description: The offer expired (server-owned expiry); it can never be accepted. Code INVITATION_EXPIRED.

calling.NotFound.description: Returned for any path the service does not expose, and for a call that does not exist in the caller's scope (indistinguishable from a call of another tenant, application or environment).

calling.ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency (database) is unavailable. Code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.

calling.SignalingAuthenticationFailed.description: Missing, malformed, expired or no longer valid signaling credential (revoked endpoint, inactive principal, revoked minting credential), or a platform API credential. Uniform for every reason. Code AUTHENTICATION_FAILED.

calling.TooManyRequests.description: RATE_LIMITED (request-rate limit) or CONCURRENT_CALL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (the environment's concurrent-call limit).

calling.Unavailable.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (database) or MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE (the media provider did not confirm the operation; the state is unchanged or queued for enforcement and reconciliation).

calling.Unprocessable.description: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (the configured media provider cannot execute or enforce the operation), PARTICIPANT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED or CALL_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

calling.ValidationError.description: Invalid query parameters (unknown or repeated parameter, out-of-range limit, malformed cursor, filter or timestamp). Code VALIDATION_ERROR.

privacy_relay.Conflict.description: CONTEXT_VERSION_CONFLICT, SESSION_VERSION_CONFLICT, CONTEXT_REFERENCE_CONFLICT, CONTEXT_NOT_ACTIVE, CONTEXT_EXPIRED, CONTEXT_REVOKED, CONTEXT_SUSPENDED, SESSION_NOT_ACTIVE or IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

privacy_relay.InvalidRequest.description: Malformed or invalid request (VALIDATION_ERROR): unknown members (a tenantId, status, version, authorization result, telephone number, provider or arbitrary policy document is refused), invalid validity, missing Idempotency-Key, inactive or foreign principals.

privacy_relay.NotFound.description: CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND / SESSION_NOT_FOUND / NOT_FOUND — identical for missing and foreign resources.

privacy_relay.Unprocessable.description: The request would broaden authority: PARTICIPANT_NOT_AUTHORIZED, DIRECTION_NOT_ALLOWED, CHANNEL_NOT_ALLOWED, STRATEGY_NOT_ALLOWED or VALIDITY_NOT_CONTAINED.
